subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.11 published dist missing reentrancy guard - reply session initialization conflicted

question: Should maintainers publish a stable hotfix/repack for the affected `2026.6.11` package, or keep the fixes in beta/main until the next stable while documenting the affected release?
rationale: The source bug is already fixed on main, but release-channel ownership determines whether stable users get a patched package now or only guidance/workarounds until the next stable release.

options.title: Publish stable package hotfix
options.body: Ship a stable package with the current writer/reply-session dist, run package parity and channel smoke proof, then close this issue with the new release evidence.

options.title: Document affected stable and wait
options.body: Leave `2026.6.11` as latest stable but publish clear operator guidance and keep this issue open until the next stable release contains the rebuilt dist.

options.title: Retire or de-emphasize 2026.6.11 stable
options.body: Move users to a validated beta or later stable once available, with explicit release notes about the affected package artifact.

recommendation.title: Publish stable package hotfix
recommendation.body: Ship a stable package with the current writer/reply-session dist, run package parity and channel smoke proof, then close this issue with the new release evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is stable release/package handling, and this account is tied to the v2026.6.11 release-head commit.
